notes:
Account summary
- Regulated healthcare AI vendor building LLM workflows on PHI (clinical notes + payer docs). Strong interest driven by public benchmark report (latency/$ + p95 stability) and wants to validate we can hit SLOs inside their own VPC.
- Primary ask: Redwood Private (customer VPC deployment) + Dedicated-like predictability (reserved capacity, predictable throughput). They explicitly do NOT want PHI leaving their AWS account.

Key contacts (Aurora)
- Head of Platform Eng (technical buyer): cares about deployment model, operability, rollback/fallback, observability.
- Security/Vendor Risk lead: running standard healthcare vendor intake (SIG-lite + pen test summary + DPA/BAA).
- Product lead for clinical summarization: cares about quality stability + “no regression” guardrails.

Why now / trigger
- Saw Redwood benchmark landing page and shared internally as evidence that “serving is the bottleneck, not the model.” They liked the focus on p95 and regional consistency vs cherry-picked tokens/sec.
- They are up for renewal on current inference approach (mix of self-hosted vLLM + occasional managed endpoints) and are hitting operational pain: noisy p95, cache/batch tuning burden, and capacity planning.

Use case + workload details (from calls)
- Workload mix: prefill-heavy summarization (long clinical docs) + smaller chat interactions for clinician prompts.
- Typical context lengths: 6k–24k tokens (long tail higher). Output: 200–800 tokens.
- Concurrency: weekdays 9am–6pm ET spike; target steady-state 150–300 concurrent requests, bursts higher during batch ingestion.
- Latency targets (stated): p95 end-to-end < 2.5s for “short chat”; for long-doc summaries they care more about throughput but want predictable p95 (avoid 10–20s outliers).
- Streaming: optional for clinician UI; must be stable (no stalls) if enabled.

Products / deployment requirements
- Redwood Private in their AWS VPC (us-east). Hard requirement: no request/response payloads, prompts, or completions leave their account.
- Customer-managed KMS keys. Prefer integration with AWS KMS; ok with envelope encryption.
- Network: private connectivity only; no public inbound.
- Data residency: US-only for PHI workloads.
- Interested in a “Dedicated-like” capacity reservation even in VPC: they want guaranteed throughput for peak clinic hours.

Security + compliance requirements (notes from vendor risk)
- HIPAA / PHI: asked directly whether Redwood will sign a BAA and what sub-processors are involved.
- Logging: “No PHI in logs” requirement. Wants confirmation of redaction defaults for request IDs and headers; asked how we prevent accidental prompt logging.
- Auditability: need audit logs for admin actions + model version changes + access to run manifests for any perf claims used in internal justification.
- Retention: controls for operational logs retention and ability to set short windows.
- SSO/SAML for Console (for any control plane UI) and RBAC.
- Pen test summary + SOC 2 report requested (standard).

Benchmark report references / questions they asked
- They cited the benchmark report as the reason they reached out, but asked “how do we know this isn’t cherry-picked?”
- Specific questions:
  - Were caching/batching enabled in published numbers? (we pointed to methodology + clarified policy + that settings are disclosed)
  - Does latency/$ normalize across different token mixes? They want a way to plug in their distribution (prefill-heavy) and see sensitivity.
  - Can we reproduce the benchmark in their VPC with our runner + their prompts (redacted) and get the same ordering?
- They requested we provide a short “how to replicate” guide for their PoC write-up.

Competitive context
- Current state: mix of self-hosted vLLM + experimenting with Bedrock; their platform team is unhappy with the operational overhead and variance under load.
- Azure OpenAI mentioned by security as “already approved vendor,” but platform team doesn’t want data egress / wants VPC-only.
- They evaluate vendors on: p95 stability under concurrency, deployment controls (pin versions, canary, fallback), and total cost at their token mix.

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2025-07-10: Inbound via benchmark report landing page CTA (notes: “need VPC/private deployment for PHI”).
- 2025-07-16: Intro call w/ Markus Klein + Lukas Meyer. Confirmed Redwood Private interest; agreed to do security deep dive.
- 2025-08-01: Shared internal benchmark methodology link + caveats; Aurora asked for a one-page summary they can send to vendor risk.
- 2025-08-12: Technical demo focused on Private architecture, routing/fallback, and observability. Follow-up questions on what telemetry leaves the VPC.
- 2026-02-24: Vendor risk pinged again after internal review; asked for BAA position + log retention controls + audit logs examples.

Deal notes / qualification
- Likely enterprise deal if we clear security. They want a committed price (monthly/annual) and clear capacity guarantees for clinic hours.
- Expansion potential: additional regions later (but US-only now).

Next steps (internal)
- Schedule 60-min security + architecture session (Aurora vendor risk + platform eng + Markus). Cover: VPC boundaries, KMS, audit logs, retention, SSO, sub-processors, and BAA path.
- Provide:
  - Redwood Private reference architecture diagram (VPC boundaries + control plane details)
  - Logging/redaction statement for Private + default telemetry settings
  - Benchmark reproducibility note: how to run a region sweep / single-region run in their VPC with run manifests
- After security green-light: propose 2-week PoC in us-east with their prompt set + target concurrency; define success metrics (p50/p95, throughput, $/1M tokens, error rate under load) and a rollback/fallback plan.

Internal-only positioning guidance
- Do not overclaim that benchmark results will match their workload 1:1. Emphasize methodology transparency + ability to reproduce + tuning via Redwood Optimize.
- Lead with: predictable p95 + economics, plus “same interface across hosted/dedicated/private” so they can start in PoC and standardize.
